title: Topographic Wetness Index (TWI)

TWI.description: Topographic wetness index (higher = wetter, more landslide-prone)

a.description: Specific contributing area (upslope drainage area per unit contour width)

applicability: Computed from LiDAR DEM. High TWI zones (convergent topography, gentle slopes below steep catchments) correlate with elevated pore pressures and increased landslide susceptibility. Used in shallow landslide susceptibility models (e.g., SHALSTAB, SINMAP).

title: Infinite Slope Stability — LiDAR-Derived Inputs
equation: FS = (c' + (γ×z×cos²β - u) × tanφ') / (γ × z × sinβ × cosβ)

z.description: Depth to failure plane (from soil thickness model or field data)

u.description: Pore water pressure at failure plane (from TWI-based or hydrologic model)

applicability: Pixel-by-pixel FS calculation using LiDAR DEM for slope angle. Pore pressure modeled from TWI, rainfall, and soil properties. Shallow translational slides (depth << length). Basis for SHALSTAB, SINMAP, TRIGRS models.
source: Skempton & DeLory (1957), adapted for GIS-based analysis

title: Inverse Velocity Failure Prediction
applicability: From Fukuzono (1985). Plot 1/v vs time from multi-epoch remote sensing (InSAR, GB-InSAR, TLS). Linear trend suggests ductile failure. Concave-up (decelerating 1/v decrease) suggests earlier failure than linear. Requires at least 3 points showing consistent acceleration.

title: Rockfall Volume from Point Cloud Comparison
equation: V_rockfall = Σᵢ |ΔZ(i)| × A_cell  for all cells in detachment zone where ΔZ < -LOD

V_rockfall.description: Volume of rock detached from source zone

ΔZ(i).description: Surface change at cell i (negative = loss)

applicability: From M3C2 or DoD comparison of pre/post-event point clouds. Volume of source zone should approximately equal deposit volume (minus fragmentation bulking factor 1.2–1.5). Applicable to individual events or cumulative rockfall inventory over time.
source: Abellán et al. (2014), Lague et al. (2013)

title: Landslide Susceptibility Index (LSI) — Logistic Regression
equation: P(landslide) = 1 / (1 + e^-(β₀ + β₁×slope + β₂×TWI + β₃×curvature + β₄×lithology + ...))

P.description: Probability of landslide occurrence in a given cell

applicability: Statistical susceptibility model trained on known landslide inventory (from LiDAR mapping). LiDAR-derived terrain attributes are the primary predictors. Validated by split-sample or cross-validation. AUC > 0.80 indicates good model performance.
source: Dai & Lee (2002), van Westen et al. (2006)

title: GB-InSAR Atmospheric Phase Correction
equation: φ_corrected = φ_measured - φ_atm  where φ_atm estimated from stable reference areas

φ_atm.description: Estimated atmospheric phase delay (from stable reflectors)

applicability: Atmospheric effects are the dominant error in GB-InSAR (path through several km of troposphere). Correction methods: use stable reference reflectors on opposite side of scene; model atmosphere from meteorological data (temperature, humidity, pressure); statistical filtering of spatially correlated signal. Residual error after correction: 0.1–0.5 mm.
source: Monserrat et al. (2014), Iglesias et al. (2014)

title: Slope Angle from DEM

∂z/∂x, ∂z/∂y.description: Partial derivatives of elevation (estimated from 3×3 neighborhood)

applicability: Computed cell-by-cell from DEM using algorithms (Horn, Zevenbergen-Thorne). DEM resolution affects slope calculation — coarser DEMs underestimate steep slopes. LiDAR DEMs (0.5–1 m) provide slope accurate to ±1–2° for smooth terrain, ±3–5° for rough terrain.

title: Empirical Landslide Runout — Volume-Dependent Travel Angle

α.description: Travel angle (fahrböschung) from head scarp to toe of deposit

H.description: Vertical drop from head scarp to distal deposit

applicability: Empirical relationship for rapid landslides and rock avalanches. Larger volume = lower travel angle = longer runout. Volume estimated from LiDAR change detection. Different relationships exist for debris flows (Rickenmann), rock avalanches (Scheidegger), and earth slides. Used for hazard zonation.
